title: Eduversal Principal Appraisal Framework v1.0
description: The Eduversal Principal Appraisal Framework v1.0 is the controlled technical implementation of Principal Appraisal: Handbook 26-27 — the fields, calculations and data mappings. If the two conflict, the Handbook governs and this framework must be corrected to match it (Handbook §1). It is a level-aware summative appraisal for partner-school principals: five areas (F1–F5) weighted into a composite annual score (0–100, mapped to an A–F predicate band), plus F_LEAD at Lead level only. There are three formal appraisal levels — Developing, Proficient and Lead. Year 1 is protected Principal Induction: it is not an appraisal level and there is no formal appraisal (Induction Charter NN1). The Chief Academic Officer / designated Academic Director (Eduversal) is the primary appraiser; the Foundation Representative / General Manager (FR/GM) is the governance-side co-reviewer and summary co-signer. Inherits the schema family of the Eduversal Teacher Appraisal Framework v2.1 — same 4-point scale, same A–F predicate bands, same Cambridge alignment block — adapted to the leadership context. Sits beside the Principal Operating Cadence (rhythm), the Principal Leadership Observation Guide (formative in-visit feedback whose visit ratings feed F2), the Stakeholder 360 and Coaching (private growth support, kept out of appraisal).

regulatory_alignment.title: Permendikdasmen 7/2025 — Penugasan Guru sebagai Kepala Sekolah
regulatory_alignment.relevance: Defines the three core duties of the principal — managerial, entrepreneurial development and supervision; observation (F2) and outcome (F4) evidence draw from these three duties. Also the current rule on appointment, term length and rotation, which affects how the induction year is treated.

regulatory_alignment.title: Permendikdasmen 21/2025 — Standar Tenaga Kependidikan (replaces Permendiknas 13/2007 — Standar Kepala Sekolah)
regulatory_alignment.relevance: The current national standard for education personnel, including heads of education units. The former five-dimension terminology of Permendiknas 13/2007 (kepribadian, manajerial, kewirausahaan, supervisi, sosial) may be used only as an internal historical crosswalk across F1–F5; it is not cited as the current regulation.

regulatory_alignment.title: Permendikdasmen 11/2025 — Beban Kerja
regulatory_alignment.relevance: 37 jam 30 menit weekly workload framework managed by the principal — F1 evidence.

regulatory_alignment.title: Permendikdasmen 13/2025 — amendment to Permendikbudristek 12/2024 on the curriculum for PAUD, primary and secondary education
regulatory_alignment.relevance: Its curriculum framework includes pembelajaran mendalam and informs instructional-leadership evidence (F2).

regulatory_alignment.title: PP 57/2021 jo. PP 4/2022 — Standar Nasional Pendidikan
regulatory_alignment.relevance: Eight national education standards (8 SNP) — F1 + F4 evidence.

regulatory_alignment.title: Cambridge Handbook for Centres
regulatory_alignment.relevance: Centre-level expectations — F2 (instructional leadership for Cambridge) and F4 (outcomes).

weights._note: These top-level weights are the Proficient (default) weights. The weights applied to a principal come from weights.by_level for their confirmed appraisal level. F_LEAD applies at Lead level only (+10%, with F1 and F2 reduced so the total still adds to 100%). There is no Year-1 / induction weight set: Year 1 is protected Principal Induction with no formal appraisal.

by_level._source: Principal Appraisal: Handbook 26-27 §6 (How the weights redistribute per level); Principal Guide 26-27 §2

F1.who: auto-aggregated from logged cadence task completion (principal_progress / weekly_progress)
F1.when: rolling all year, from the principal's confirmed F1 scoring window (26-27: begins on the formal launch date; no retrospective penalty for July–August — Handbook §14)

F2.who: Chief Academic Officer / designated Academic Director (or an assigned observer)
F2.when: At least two scheduled visits a year: Visit 1 in Sept–Oct and Visit 2 in Feb–Apr. Where practicable, only the Sept–Oct visit is paired with an on-site School Appraisal visit; the Feb–Apr visit is scheduled separately, because both on-site School Appraisal visits take place in Semester 1. The two appraisal systems keep separate evidence, records and decisions (Handbook §7, §12).

F3.who: anonymous respondents (staff / parent representatives / student-council representatives)
F3.when: Two planned cycles: the mid-year cycle (W17) is formative only and does not enter F3; the late-year / year-end cycle (W38) is the official summative F3 evidence (Handbook §7).

F5.who: Principal (self); the appraiser rates depth and honesty
F5.when: Two termly self-assessments plus an annual reflection

score_conversion.rule: Each area's mean rubric rating (1–4) is converted to a 0–100 area score as (mean rating ÷ 4) × 100. The level weights are then applied to the area scores to give the composite score (0–100).
score_conversion.f2_mapping: F2 visit ratings are recorded as Established / Developing / Not Observed. For aggregation E = 4 and D = 2; Not Observed is excluded rather than scored (Handbook §5).
score_conversion.source: Appraisal Suite: Master Overview 26-27 — Principal Appraisal uses 'the same 4-point scale as Teacher Appraisal', whose conversion is '(mean rubric rating ÷ 4) × 100 before framework weights are applied'. The Principal Appraisal Handbook states the conversion only by this reference.
score_conversion.completeness_gate: No final composite, band or recommendation is issued while F5 is incomplete (both termly self-assessments + the annual reflection) or while fewer than two valid F2 observation records exist (Handbook §4, §14; Appraiser Guide §4, §6).

predicate_bands_note: Bands are half-open: a composite of exactly 86 is A and 85.99 is B. 'max' is the lower edge of the next band up and is exclusive (Handbook §5; Master Overview 26-27).

level_visibility.note: Each item carries a 'visible_from' field giving the minimum level at which it appears. Items visible from 'developing' appear at every formal level; items visible from 'lead' appear only at Lead (the F_LEAD area). There is no scored 'induction' level: Year 1 is protected Principal Induction, recorded through the binary Induction Completion Certificate (Induction Charter NN1, NN5). Appraisal level is confirmed by Eduversal (the Executive Director), not fixed by years alone.

weight_redistribution.developing: F1: 0.20, F2: 0.45, F3: 0.15, F4: 0.15, F5: 0.05 (newer principals: leadership observation weighted more heavily)
weight_redistribution.lead: F1: 0.20, F2: 0.35, F3: 0.15, F4: 0.15, F5: 0.05, F_LEAD: 0.10 (F_LEAD added; F1 and F2 reduced so the total still adds to 1.00)

year_to_level_mapping.year_1: Protected Principal Induction — not an appraisal level and no formal appraisal (Induction Charter NN1). At the end of Year 1 the Eduversal Induction Coordinator signs the induction off as completed / withdrew; on 'completed' the principal receives the Induction Completion Certificate — binary, no score (Induction Charter NN5).
year_to_level_mapping.year_2: First formal appraisal at the end of Year 2, at the Developing level.

frameworks.title: Operating Cadence Compliance
frameworks.description: Auto-aggregated evidence of how consistently the principal runs the Principal Operating Cadence (83 tasks across P1–P8): daily huddles, weekly walkthroughs, monthly RKAS reviews, termly EDS cycles, annual vision-and-mission reviews. Measures frequency and fidelity from logged task completion and on-time evidence. 26-27 transition: the scored F1 window begins on the principal's formal launch date; July–August 2026 cannot be scored as missing or late, and evidence must never be recreated or back-filled (Handbook §14).
frameworks.items_note: Items pulled from weekly_progress and principal_progress collections via aggregation. No subjective scoring at this level — completion data + evidence-quality flags drive the score.

items.title: Compliance-tier task completion rate

rubric.1: <70% of compliance-tier tasks (43 tasks) completed with evidence on time

items.data_source: principal_progress aggregated against principal-operating-cadence.json compliance-tier tasks

items.title: Core-tier task completion rate
items.data_source: principal_progress aggregated against principal-operating-cadence.json core-tier tasks

rubric.1: Evidence missing or late on >25% of completed tasks
rubric.3: Evidence current on >=90% of tasks within 24h-48h windows
rubric.4: Evidence current on 100% of tasks; archive immaculate

frameworks.title: Leadership Observation
frameworks.description: Score derived from the principal's valid scheduled leadership-observation records (principal-observation-rubric.json). P1–P8 visit ratings (E = Established, D = Developing, N = Not Observed) are mapped for aggregation (E = 4, D = 2, N excluded) and averaged across visits. At least two valid scheduled visits a year — Visit 1 Sept–Oct, Visit 2 Feb–Apr; only the Sept–Oct visit is paired with an on-site School Appraisal visit where practicable. A pre-launch visit counts only if the principal was told in advance it would contribute to Principal Appraisal, the P1–P8 framework was used and a valid record exists; otherwise it is formative context only (Handbook §14).
frameworks.valid_record_rule: A valid F2 record is a submitted principal_observations document of a scheduled appraisal visit in the Sept–Oct or Feb–Apr window, marked as counting toward F2. The annual appraisal needs at least two.

frameworks.title: Stakeholder 360° Feedback
frameworks.description: Anonymous feedback from staff (60% within F3), parent representatives (25%) and student-council representatives (15%), against the same eight leadership focus areas with audience-tailored questions. A cohort needs at least 5 respondents to be scored; a below-threshold cohort is reported as 'insufficient response' and its weight is redistributed proportionally to the cohorts that met the threshold. Only the late-year / year-end (summative) cycle enters F3; the mid-year cycle is formative only (Handbook §7, §8).

items.title: Staff feedback aggregate
items.data_source: principal_360_aggregates/{cycleId} (year-end W38 cycle only) cohortStats where respondent_type=staff

items.title: Parent representative feedback
items.data_source: principal_360_aggregates/{cycleId} (year-end W38 cycle only) cohortStats where respondent_type=parent

items.title: Student-council representative feedback
items.data_source: principal_360_aggregates/{cycleId} (year-end W38 cycle only) cohortStats where respondent_type=student

frameworks.anonymisation_protocol: Below-threshold cohorts are reported as 'insufficient response'. Individual responses are never disclosed to the principal or the Foundation Representative; appraisers use aggregate results only. The F3 area score is never shared with the FR/GM or the yayasan.

frameworks.title: Outcome Indicators
frameworks.description: Auto-pulled from Academic Hub dashboards at the End-of-Year Conference: EASE Growth (in 2026–27 a Version 1 baseline, read alongside the other measures), the Cambridge results trajectory, and Rapor Pendidikan and national benchmarks. General Student / Parent / Staff Satisfaction Surveys are contextual triangulation only and do not create an F4 score. Other school indicators (attendance, PD, strategic goals, climate, budget/compliance) may give context for the conversation but do not become F4 components unless this framework is formally updated (Handbook §4). F4 is the school's collective performance under the principal's leadership, capped at 15% because a principal does not control every factor.

items.title: EASE Growth position (Version 1 baseline in 2026–27)
items.data_source: EASE Growth results — Academic Hub /ease-growth-results (school baseline by grade band)
items.rating_guidance: 2026–27 is Version 1: EASE Growth results are a baseline, never a growth score, and there is no growth or network-ranking rubric in Version 1. Rate this item on the 4-point scale from the school's baseline read alongside the other F4 measures, and write the interpretation (baseline → current result → evidence source → interpretation → action → review point).

items.title: Cambridge results trajectory
items.data_source: Cambridge results — Academic Hub /cambridge-results (year-on-year grade distribution)

rubric.1: Significant decline in grade distribution OR Cambridge findings flagged

items.title: Rapor Pendidikan + national benchmarks
items.data_source: Rapor Pendidikan (raporpendidikan.kemdikbud.go.id) and national benchmarks — current release

contextual_only: General Student / Parent / Staff Satisfaction Surveys — contextual triangulation only; never an F4 item (Handbook §4; Principal Guide 26-27; Master Overview 26-27).

frameworks.title: Self-Assessment & Reflection
frameworks.description: Two termly self-assessments plus an annual evidence-grounded reflection, completed by the principal; the appraiser rates depth and honesty. Low weight (5%) but required evidence: if the self-assessments and the annual reflection are incomplete, the annual appraisal remains incomplete and no final composite, band or recommendation is issued until F5 is completed (Handbook §4). Coaching session content and coaching participation metadata do not feed F5 (Handbook §2, §10).

rubric.3: Both termly self-assessments completed with substantive narrative
rubric.4: Both completed with evidence-grounded narrative referencing specific cadence tasks and observation findings

rubric.3: Substantive narrative referencing specific cadence completion + observation findings
rubric.4: Reflective narrative connects the F1–F4 evidence to clear next-year goals (Handbook §11)

frameworks.title: Network Leadership Contribution
frameworks.description: Lead level only (roughly Year 7+). Adds 10%; items measure mentoring of other principals, sharing exemplars and helping newer Cambridge centres mature. Scored once a year by the Executive Director. Any mentoring of a partner principal follows the induction rule that the mentor holds active Eduversal Mentor Certification before assignment (Induction Charter NN3).
frameworks.weight_note: +0.10 at Lead level only; F1 and F2 are reduced (to 0.20 and 0.35) so the total still adds to 1.00.

items.title: Active mentoring of partner-school principal mentee(s)
items.data_source: induction_assignments where mentorUid = principalUid AND status=active

rubric.3: One active mentoring assignment, with sessions held on the agreed cadence
rubric.4: Multiple assignments OR exceptional mentee outcomes documented

items.title: Network-level contribution (cross-school workshops, exemplar sharing)
items.data_source: Eduversal-network event participation log, exemplar contributions to network resource library

items.title: Cambridge Centre maturity contribution
items.applies_when: school is Cambridge Approved Centre at maturity-2 or above
items.data_source: Cambridge Centre evaluation, mentoring of pre-Centre partner schools

narrative_fields.label: Headline Strength
narrative_fields.description: The single most notable leadership strength evidenced this year. Specific, evidence-anchored.
narrative_fields.author: primary_appraiser

narrative_fields.label: Priority Development Area
narrative_fields.description: The single most important area to grow next year, framed as an opportunity, not a deficit (Handbook §9).
narrative_fields.author: primary_appraiser

narrative_fields.label: Recommendation
narrative_fields.description: One of three choices: 'continue' (the normal outcome of a healthy year), 'development_plan' (continue with a structured, supported plan — a supportive step, not a demotion) or 'non_renewal' (the last resort, after genuine support). The composite and band inform the recommendation but do not produce it automatically (Handbook §9).
narrative_fields.author: primary_appraiser

narrative_fields.label: Agreed Next-Year Goals
narrative_fields.description: Two or three specific, outcome-based goals for next year, tied to leadership competency advancement. Where practical, each goal names a baseline, the intended change, the evidence source that will show progress, and a review point (Handbook §9).
narrative_fields.author: primary_appraiser (agreed with the principal)

narrative_fields.label: Principal's Reflection
narrative_fields.description: The principal's own response to the appraisal, written by the principal after sign-off. Acknowledging the appraisal is not the same as agreeing with it — the principal keeps the right to dispute.
narrative_fields.author: principal

narrative_fields.label: Confidential Note
narrative_fields.description: Eduversal-internal only — not shown to the principal, the Foundation Representative or the yayasan. Used sparingly, for safeguarding concerns, governance issues or an escalation flag; keep it factual. Stored separately from the appraisal record.
narrative_fields.author: primary_appraiser

metadata_fields.label: Appraisal Level
metadata_fields.note: Confirmed by Eduversal before the scored cycle begins. Year-1 principals are not appraised.

metadata_fields.label: Primary appraiser (Chief Academic Officer / designated Academic Director)
Visit dates of the valid F2 observation records (at least two)
360 cycle ID contributing to F3 (the late-year / year-end summative cycle only)
Formal launch date (written confirmation of level, primary appraiser, evidence window and calendar)

charter_compliance.NN1: No formal appraisal during induction year (Year 1). End-of-Year-1 produces induction completion certificate ONLY (binary). First formal appraisal end of Year 2 at 'developing' level.
charter_compliance.NN2: The principal's induction journal never feeds this appraisal: Eduversal never reads named journal entries (the induction_journal collection is list-blocked), and no F-item data_source draws on journal data (Handbook §10).
charter_compliance.NN3: F_LEAD-1 mentoring evidence: the mentor of a partner principal must hold active Eduversal Mentor Certification before any mentee assignment is created. No separate endorsement document is required (Induction Module: Principal 26-27 §2.2).
charter_compliance.yayasan_triplet_boundary: A Principal Appraisal Framework rule (Handbook §10) — not an Induction Charter Non-Negotiable. The Foundation Representative / General Manager and the yayasan receive only the approved summary triplet (composite score + predicate band + recommendation) plus the agreed next-year goals. They never see item-level scores, P1–P8 observation notes, F3 area scores, individual 360 responses, coaching content or journal content. The FR/GM co-signs the summary; they do not write the record or re-score evidence.
charter_compliance.coaching_exclusion: A Principal Appraisal Framework rule (Handbook §2, §10): coaching session content and coaching participation metadata do not feed any appraisal score or F5. The appraiser does not see coaching records.
charter_compliance.school_appraisal_separation: Principal Appraisal and School Appraisal may share a visit trip, but their evidence, ratings, records and decisions stay separate (Handbook §7, §12, §14).

document_fields.principalReflection: string (PNF5 — written by the principal after sign-off)

sourcesUsed._excluded: Coaching sessions, induction journals and induction observations are never a source.

governance_summary.purpose: The only appraisal content the Foundation Representative / General Manager and the yayasan receive (Handbook §10).

coverage.note: Each framework item carries cambridge_school_leader_refs[] linking to the 25 CSL 2023 standards covered by competency_framework/leaders. Aggregate coverage matches the leaders track.

schema_lineage: Inherits the schema family of Eduversal Teacher Appraisal Framework v2.1 (appraisal-framework-v2.json). Same scoring_scale + predicate_bands + level_visibility + cambridge_alignment block shape. Adapted to leadership context. Where this file diverges from v2.1, it does so for principal-specific reasons (F2 data_source = principal_observations not direct observation; F4 = school outcomes aggregate; F_LEAD = network contribution layer).
